# Demo dataset figures

**Generated by `make docs-numbers`. Do not edit by hand.**

These are the headline figures the README and the concept docs refer to. They describe a rolling 90-day window over a synthetic dataset, so they move when the data is reseeded — which is exactly why they live in a generated file rather than in prose. If a number here disagrees with something written elsewhere in the repository, this file is right and the prose is stale.

**The dataset is synthetic.** Nothing below describes real customers, real sending, or real outcomes.

---

## Routing SLA

Over the last 90 days, **604** lead-event assignments carry an SLA.

| Measure | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Assignments with an SLA | 604 |
| Met the SLA | 474 (78.7% of those decided) |
| Touched late | 106 |
| Never touched at all | 22 |
| Still pending (clock running) | 2 |
| Median time to first touch | 4.4 h |

**Late**, **never touched** and **pending** are counted separately on purpose. A late touch is a process problem; an assignment nobody ever touched is a lead that was routed into silence; and an assignment whose clock is still running is neither. Collapsing the three hides the second inside the first and inflates the hit rate with the third.

## Experiment: provocative subject

Verdict **treatment_better** — recommendation: **do_not_ship**.

| Metric | Control | Treatment | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| **reply** (primary) | 20.68% (n=266) | 36.96% (n=276) | +16.3 pp, p = 2.95e-05 |
| Hard bounce rate (guardrail) | 1.88% | 1.09% (95% CI 0.37%–3.15%) | ok |
| Unsubscribe rate (guardrail) | 0.00% | 2.90% (95% CI 1.48%–5.61%) | **breach** |
| Spam complaint rate (guardrail) | 0.00% | 0.72% (95% CI 0.20%–2.60%) | **watch** |
| Negative reply rate (guardrail) | 2.63% | 10.14% (95% CI 7.11%–14.27%) | **breach** |

This is the case the experiment engine exists for: the treatment wins the primary metric decisively and is still rejected, because a guardrail breached. A system that ships the winner here is a system that burns the list.

## Data quality

**504** open issues across **12** rules.

| Rule | Open |
| --- | ---: |
| `stale_enrichment` | 310 |
| `invalid_email` | 81 |
| `missing_employee_count` | 35 |
| `duplicate_contact` | 18 |
| `provider_conflict` | 15 |
| `orphan_contact` | 14 |
| `missing_domain` | 9 |
| `lifecycle_conflict` | 8 |
| `bad_external_id` | 6 |
| `duplicate_account` | 6 |
| `invalid_pipeline_transition` | 2 |

`provider_conflict` is the one worth reading: those are fields where two providers materially disagree and GTMOS refused to pick a winner on confidence alone. It raises an issue instead, which is a deliberately worse experience than silently overwriting and a much better outcome.

## Deliverability

Risk score **41/100**, verdict **throttle** — Halve the volume and fix the list before adding any.

| Signal | Rate | 95% CI | Status | Proven? |
| --- | ---: | :---: | --- | --- |
| Spam complaint rate | 0.40% | 0.14%–1.17% | watch | yes |
| Hard bounce rate | 2.61% | 2.15%–3.16% | watch | yes |
| Unsubscribe rate | 1.33% | 0.73%–2.44% | watch | not proven |
| Reply rate | 5.01% | 4.37%–5.75% | ok | yes |
| Unsendable addresses on the list | 0.72% | — | ok | yes |
| Unverified addresses on the list | 12.73% | — | watch | yes |

The **Proven?** column is the point. A rate over its threshold whose confidence interval still reaches back under it is *not proven and not ignorable*, and the assessment says so rather than rounding a wide interval into a verdict.

GTMOS has no mailbox and sends nothing. These are inputs to a capacity calculator and a list-health assessment, not a description of infrastructure that exists.
